input.title: PreflightRequest
input.description: A payment you are considering, in your own terms. Every protocol value — the policy hash, the token contract, the hashes of the things you describe below, the nonce, the endpoint — is derived server-side from production state and returned to you, so there is nothing here you have to look up first.

policyId.description: The id of a policy registered on the PolicyRegistry contract, as a decimal string. It names the spending rules this request is judged against.

useDefaultPolicy.description: Use the policy this account has marked as its default. Send this or policyId, not neither — a request that silently fell back to a default would be a request whose limits nobody chose.

provider.description: The provider you want to pay, by its registered id.

capability.description: What you want that provider to do, by its registered capability id.

task.description: What this payment is for, in a sentence a person would recognise.

maxSpend.description: The most you will spend, in DISPLAY units — "20.00", not base units.

currency.description: The settlement currency's symbol. It must be one this network actually settles.

deadline.description: After this the request is stale and must be rebuilt rather than replayed.

recipient.description: Optional. Constrains who may be paid. Without it, the recipient must come from a resolved quote.

parameters.description: Optional. The structured parameters that will be sent to the provider. Hashed and committed.

acceptance.description: Optional. What "delivered" will mean, committed NOW so that verification later has something to compare against. Without it the task text is used.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional. Makes a retry of an identical request resolve to the same intent rather than creating a second one.

buyerAgentId.description: Optional and temporary. Which agent is spending is a property of an account; send it explicitly until your wallet is bound to one.

workerAgentId.description: Optional and temporary. Which agent is being paid is a property of the provider's registration; send it explicitly until that binding exists.

reasons.description: Why, in the policy's own terms.

ruleTrace.description: Every rule evaluated, in order, with its verdict. The audit trail of the decision.

intentHash.description: The hash of the intent that was judged.

receiptRef.description: The receipt this decision was written to, when a receipt writer is wired.

policyId.description: The id of a policy registered on the PolicyRegistry contract, as a decimal string. It names the spending rules this request is judged against.

intent.title: SpendIntent
intent.description: The bounded object a spend decision is made about. Eleven of these fields are hashed together into the intentHash that the receipt commits to; the remaining five are the operational values the rules read.

owner.description: The address that owns the policy this intent is judged against.

buyerAgentId.description: The ERC-8004 agent id of the agent doing the spending. Sent as a DECIMAL STRING, not a JSON number — JSON numbers cannot carry uint256 without losing precision, so a number here is refused rather than rounded.

workerAgentId.description: The ERC-8004 agent id of the agent being paid. Sent as a DECIMAL STRING, not a JSON number — JSON numbers cannot carry uint256 without losing precision, so a number here is refused rather than rounded.

token.description: The ERC-20 the payment settles in.

maxAmount.description: The ceiling for this payment, in the token's BASE UNITS. Sent as a DECIMAL STRING, not a JSON number — JSON numbers cannot carry uint256 without losing precision, so a number here is refused rather than rounded.

taskHash.description: A hash of the task description this payment is for.

acceptanceHash.description: A hash of the acceptance criteria delivery will later be judged against.

schemaHash.description: A hash of the schema the delivered result must conform to.

policyHash.description: The stored hash of the policy named by policyId. Must match exactly.

deadline.description: Unix seconds after which this intent is no longer valid. Sent as a DECIMAL STRING, not a JSON number — JSON numbers cannot carry uint256 without losing precision, so a number here is refused rather than rounded.

nonce.description: A value that makes this intent distinct from an otherwise identical one. Sent as a DECIMAL STRING, not a JSON number — JSON numbers cannot carry uint256 without losing precision, so a number here is refused rather than rounded.

endpoint.description: The absolute URL the payment is for. Must be absolute, including the scheme.

paramsHash.description: A hash of the parameters that will be sent to that endpoint.

recipientAddress.description: The address that will receive the funds.

category.description: The spend category, as your policy names it. Used by category rules.

amount.description: The amount in DISPLAY units, as a JSON NUMBER. This is the one field that must not be a string — every other numeric field above is a decimal string. The inversion is load-bearing: maxAmount is a uint256 ceiling in base units, and this is the human-scale figure the budget rules read.

intentHash.description: The hash every later step refers to.

canonicalIntent.description: Exactly the values that were hashed.

txHash.description: The confirmed registerPolicy transaction YOUR wallet sent.

owner.description: Read from the PolicyRegistered event, never from the caller.

refused.title: Sync a registration somebody else made

predecessors.what: An Untch account, established by proving a wallet.
predecessors.why: Authority here is a verified wallet and nothing else. Without one there is no owner for a policy, no subject for an approval, and no account a marketplace identity can be bound to.
predecessors.obtainableBy: POST /consumer/account/link/start, sign the message, then POST /consumer/account/link/complete

predecessors.what: A policy draft, and a confirmed registerPolicy transaction for it.
predecessors.why: The draft holds the rules the anchored hash is checked against; the transaction is what made you the owner.
predecessors.obtainableBy: POST /consumer/policies/draft, then send the returned transaction from your own wallet

sideEffects.what: Stores the policy and links it to this account.
Sets it as the default when the account has none.

refusals.when: no account session accompanied the request
no such draft, or it belongs to another account
the on-chain owner is not a policy-authority wallet of this account
the draft's rules do not hash to what the transaction anchored
no PolicyRegistered event could be read from that transaction

description.what: Chooses which policy answers when a request names none. For an account owner holding more than one policy.
description.provide: You provide: policyId (string).
description.receive: You receive: the chosen default, after checking the account can actually sign for it.

predecessors.what: An Untch account, established by proving a wallet.
predecessors.why: Authority here is a verified wallet and nothing else. Without one there is no owner for a policy, no subject for an approval, and no account a marketplace identity can be bound to.
predecessors.obtainableBy: POST /consumer/account/link/start, sign the message, then POST /consumer/account/link/complete

predecessors.what: A registered spend policy, and its numeric policyId.
predecessors.why: Every decision this service makes is a comparison against a policy. Without one there is nothing to compare to, and the request is refused rather than judged.
predecessors.obtainableBy: POST /consumer/policies/draft to build the unsigned registration, send that transaction from your own wallet, then POST /consumer/policies/sync. The policy's owner is whoever sent it — Untch does not relay the call and cannot.

sideEffects.what: Changes which policy an unqualified request resolves to.

refusals.when: no account session accompanied the request
no such policy on this account
the policy is paused
the policy has expired
no wallet on this account owns it

description.what: Approves or rejects one escalated action, naming the exact payment it authorises. For the account owner, through a wallet-backed session.
description.provide: You provide: decision (string); approvalDigest (string).
description.receive: You receive: the resolved state, and an explicit statement of whether anything was paid.

approvalDigest.description: REQUIRED. The digest you were shown, covering intent, quote, amount, asset, provider, capability, recipient, policy, version, nonce and expiry. A decision without it is not a decision: a re-quote changes the digest, and approving the old one would agree to a number you were never shown.

outcome.description: APPROVED_AWAITING_EXECUTION when provider execution is disabled.

paid.description: Whether money actually moved. Approving is not paying.

repeat.description: True when this repeated an identical earlier decision.

predecessors.what: An Untch account, established by proving a wallet.
predecessors.why: Authority here is a verified wallet and nothing else. Without one there is no owner for a policy, no subject for an approval, and no account a marketplace identity can be bound to.
predecessors.obtainableBy: POST /consumer/account/link/start, sign the message, then POST /consumer/account/link/complete

predecessors.what: A pending approval request, raised because an action exceeded the policy's automatic-approval threshold.
predecessors.why: There is nothing to decide until the policy engine asks.
predecessors.obtainableBy: GET /consumer/approvals lists them; they are created by the decision path, never by a caller

predecessors.what: A verified channel binding, for any decision arriving from Telegram or Discord.
predecessors.why: A callback carries a platform identity, which authorises nothing until that identity has been bound to an account. Email never gains a decision path at all: a sender address is forged trivially, so email carries a link to an authenticated session.
predecessors.obtainableBy: start the binding from an authenticated dashboard session; production sending stays disabled until the channel credential is rotated (see /internal/credential-state)

sideEffects.what: Records a decision bound to the exact payment digest.
Resolves the approval request. It does NOT execute anything.

refusals.when: no account session accompanied the request
approvalDigest was omitted
no such approval, or it belongs to another account
the digest no longer describes this payment — the quote changed
already resolved, or superseded by a re-quote
this actor already answered, and differently
the approval expired before it was answered
